request.prompt:
Job T01: usp_load_dim_customer (tsql), legacy file estate/tsql/T01_usp_load_dim_customer.sql (SHA-256 d38c02712a8ae80f9e6e8fff845b41ac7d89026778fc03455b34ded21bba4dc6).
Customer dimension, one row per CRM customer.
Invocations, in order: run: AsOfDate=2025-12-31.

Legacy code:
/*==============================================================================
  Job      : dw.usp_load_dim_customer
  Purpose  : Customer dimension for the marketing and pricing teams. One row
             per CRM customer with the customer's current details from the
             CRM extract, plus sales region, Eircode check, initials and
             segment flags for campaigns and the pricing models.
  Output   : dw.dim_customer (truncated and reloaded on every run)
  Author   : DOC

  Change log
    2013-05-20  DOC   Initial version
    2014-11-03  DOC   Sales region from county for the regional reports (CR-0412)
    2015-01-26  DOC   full_name and initials for the mail merge (CR-0538)
    2016-02-18  AMcG  Eircode added, with a format check (CR-0877)
    2017-09-07  AMcG  email_shared_count for the marketing duplicate review
                      (CR-1190)
    2018-05-21  AMcG  Opt-in defaults to N when the customer was never asked
                      (GDPR, CR-1342)
    2019-03-25  SR    age_at_join for the pricing models (CR-1564)
    2019-11-04  KB    CRM extract is now change data capture: one row per
                      saved version, keep the current one (CR-1702)
    2020-10-12  SR    is_standard_segment for the renewal campaign (CR-1841)
    2021-06-14  KB    Logging through etl.usp_log_step (CR-2003)
==============================================================================*/
SET NOCOUNT ON;
GO
IF OBJECT_ID(N'dw.dim_customer', N'U') IS NULL
CREATE TABLE dw.dim_customer (
    customer_id          INT            NOT NULL,
    first_name           NVARCHAR(40)   NOT NULL,
    last_name            NVARCHAR(60)   NOT NULL,
    full_name            NVARCHAR(101)  NOT NULL,
    initials             NVARCHAR(2)    NOT NULL,
    email                VARCHAR(120)   NULL,
    email_shared_count   INT            NOT NULL,
    date_of_birth        DATE           NULL,
    age_at_join          INT            NULL,
    address_line1        NVARCHAR(100)  NULL,
    town                 NVARCHAR(50)   NULL,
    county               VARCHAR(30)    NULL,
    region               VARCHAR(12)    NOT NULL,
    eircode              VARCHAR(10)    NULL,
    eircode_valid        CHAR(1)        NOT NULL,
    segment_code         CHAR(4)        NULL,
    is_standard_segment  CHAR(1)        NOT NULL,
    marketing_opt_in     CHAR(1)        NOT NULL,
    customer_since       DATE           NOT NULL,
    source_system        VARCHAR(10)    NOT NULL,
    version_count        INT            NOT NULL,
    record_updated_at    DATETIME2(0)   NOT NULL,
    as_of_date           DATE           NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT pk_dim_customer PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED (customer_id)
);
GO
CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE dw.usp_load_dim_customer
    @AsOfDate DATE
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;

    DECLARE @job_name  VARCHAR(128) = 'dw.usp_load_dim_customer',
            @rows      INT,
            @err_msg   NVARCHAR(4000),
            @err_no    INT;

    BEGIN TRY
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'start', @status = 'STARTED';

        IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#customer_versions') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #customer_versions;
        IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#customer') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #customer;

        /* 1. Customer versions saved up to the reporting date. The CRM extract
              writes a new row every time a record is saved. */
        SELECT  c.customer_id,
                c.first_name,
                c.last_name,
                c.email,
                c.date_of_birth,
                c.address_line1,
                c.town,
                c.county,
                c.eircode,
                c.segment_code,
                c.marketing_opt_in,
                c.customer_since,
                c.source_system,
                c.updated_at,
                c._row_seq,
                COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY c.customer_id) AS version_count
        INTO    #customer_versions
        FROM    stg.customers c WITH (NOLOCK)
        WHERE   CAST(c.updated_at AS DATE) <= @AsOfDate;

        SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'customer versions', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;

        /* 2. Keep the current version of each customer */
        SELECT  v.*
        INTO    #customer
        FROM   (SELECT  cv.*,
                        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cv.customer_id
                                           ORDER BY cv.updated_at, cv._row_seq) AS version_no
                FROM    #customer_versions cv) v
        WHERE   v.version_no = 1;

        SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'current versions', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;

        /* 3. Reload the dimension */
        BEGIN TRANSACTION;

        TRUNCATE TABLE dw.dim_customer;

        INSERT INTO dw.dim_customer
               (customer_id, first_name, last_name, full_name, initials, email,
                email_shared_count, date_of_birth, age_at_join, address_line1, town,
                county, region, eircode, eircode_valid, segment_code, is_standard_segment,
                marketing_opt_in, customer_since, source_system, version_count,
                record_updated_at, as_of_date)
        SELECT  k.customer_id,
                RTRIM(k.first_name),
                k.last_name,
                RTRIM(k.first_name) + N' ' + RTRIM(k.last_name),
                UPPER(SUBSTRING(k.first_name, 0, 2) + SUBSTRING(k.last_name, 0, 2)),
                k.email,
                CASE WHEN k.email IS NULL THEN 0
                     ELSE COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY k.email) END,
                k.date_of_birth,
                DATEDIFF(YEAR, k.date_of_birth, k.customer_since),
                k.address_line1,
                k.town,
                k.county,
                -- sales regions as agreed with distribution (CR-0412)
                CASE WHEN k.county IN ('Dublin', 'Kildare', 'Meath', 'Wicklow', 'Louth', 'Wexford') THEN 'EAST'
                     WHEN k.county IN ('Cork', 'Kerry', 'Limerick', 'Tipperary', 'Waterford', 'Kilkenny', 'Carlow') THEN 'SOUTH'
                     WHEN k.county IN ('Galway', 'Mayo', 'Clare', 'Roscommon') THEN 'WEST'
                     WHEN k.county IN ('Donegal', 'Sligo', 'Leitrim', 'Cavan', 'Monaghan') THEN 'NORTH-WEST'
                     WHEN k.county IN ('Westmeath', 'Longford', 'Offaly', 'Laois') THEN 'MIDLANDS'
                     ELSE 'UNKNOWN'
                END,
                k.eircode,
                -- routing key (3) and unique identifier (4), keyed with or without the space
                CASE WHEN LEN(k.eircode) = 7 THEN 'Y'
                     WHEN LEN(k.eircode) = 8 AND SUBSTRING(k.eircode, 4, 1) = ' ' THEN 'Y'
                     ELSE 'N'
                END,
                k.segment_code,
                CASE WHEN k.segment_code = 'STD' THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END,
                ISNULL(k.marketing_opt_in, 'N'),
                k.customer_since,
                UPPER(RTRIM(k.source_system)),
                k.version_count,
                k.updated_at,
                @AsOfDate
        FROM    #customer k;

        SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;

        COMMIT TRANSACTION;

        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'dw.dim_customer', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'SUCCESS';
    END TRY
    BEGIN CATCH
        IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;

        SELECT  @err_msg = ERROR_MESSAGE(),
                @err_no  = ERROR_NUMBER();

        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'FAILED',
             @message = @err_msg, @error_number = @err_no;
        THROW;
    END CATCH
END;
GO

request.system_prompt:
Translate one legacy T-SQL (SQL Server 2022) job to PySpark 4.2. Your output must reproduce the legacy output EXACTLY, record for record and value for value, bugs included: reconciliation compares every row and column with the legacy engine's own output.

Write one Python module:
- Imports only from pyspark (pyspark.sql, pyspark.sql.functions as F, pyspark.sql.types as T, pyspark.sql.Window), datetime, decimal, math, re, functools and typing.
- Exactly this entry point: def run(spark: SparkSession, inputs: dict[str, DataFrame], params: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, DataFrame]:
- inputs holds every input table by its legacy name in lower case (e.g. "stg.claims"); params holds the parameters as text (e.g. params["AsOfDate"] == "2025-12-31").
- Return a dict from each output's legacy name to a DataFrame with the output's columns. The harness then casts each column to the contract type shown, as the legacy table's insert would (so a decimal(38,6) value stored into decimal(14,2) is rounded half up).
- Never do I/O or reach engine internals: no spark.read, .write, saveAsTable, spark.conf, RDDs, UDFs, .cache(), getattr, eval, open, os or sys. spark.sql, F.expr and selectExpr only with plain string literals (no f-strings).
- Use only constants that appear in the legacy code, the parameters, or a trap card's fix guidance (format patterns, collation names). Never hard-code data values.
- Reproduce every legacy behaviour exactly, including anything that looks like a bug: never fix it. Mark each line that reproduces a suspected bug with a "# LANSH-DEFECT: <what>" comment and list the bug in defects.
- Row order: Spark has none. Wherever the result depends on order (first or last row, a running value, a cursor, NODUPKEY, RETAIN, LAG), sort on the legacy ORDER BY and then _row_seq, which every source table has in its original row order.
- Spark runs with ANSI mode on: overflow and invalid casts raise errors, and a division by zero raises; use try_divide or a guard only where the legacy engine returns NULL.

structured_output.code:
"""Job T01: dw.usp_load_dim_customer (legacy T-SQL, SQL Server 2022) migrated to PySpark.

Customer dimension, one row per CRM customer. Output dw.dim_customer is fully
reloaded on every run. Reproduces the legacy behaviour exactly, including
suspected bugs (marked LANSH-DEFECT).
"""
import datetime

from pyspark.sql import DataFrame, SparkSession, Window
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def _ci(col):
    # SQL Server default collation: case-insensitive, trailing spaces ignored in comparisons
    return F.lower(F.rtrim(col))


def run(spark: SparkSession, inputs: dict[str, DataFrame], params: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, DataFrame]:
    as_of = datetime.date.fromisoformat(params["AsOfDate"])
    c = inputs["stg.customers"]

    # 1. Versions saved up to the reporting date
    v = c.where(F.to_date(F.col("updated_at")) <= F.lit(as_of))
    v = v.withColumn(
        "version_count",
        F.count(F.lit(1)).over(Window.partitionBy("customer_id")),
    )

    # 2. "Keep the current version" -- legacy orders ascending, so it keeps the OLDEST version
    w = Window.partitionBy("customer_id").orderBy(F.col("updated_at").asc(), F.col("_row_seq").asc())  # LANSH-DEFECT: ascending order keeps the oldest version, not the current one
    k = v.withColumn("version_no", F.row_number().over(w)).where(F.col("version_no") == 1)

    # 3. Dimension columns
    email = F.col("email")
    email_count = F.count(F.lit(1)).over(Window.partitionBy(_ci(email)))

    county = _ci(F.col("county"))
    east = [s.lower() for s in ['Dublin', 'Kildare', 'Meath', 'Wicklow', 'Louth', 'Wexford']]
    south = [s.lower() for s in ['Cork', 'Kerry', 'Limerick', 'Tipperary', 'Waterford', 'Kilkenny', 'Carlow']]
    west = [s.lower() for s in ['Galway', 'Mayo', 'Clare', 'Roscommon']]
    north_west = [s.lower() for s in ['Donegal', 'Sligo', 'Leitrim', 'Cavan', 'Monaghan']]
    midlands = [s.lower() for s in ['Westmeath', 'Longford', 'Offaly', 'Laois']]
    region = (
        F.when(county.isin(east), F.lit('EAST'))
        .when(county.isin(south), F.lit('SOUTH'))
        .when(county.isin(west), F.lit('WEST'))
        .when(county.isin(north_west), F.lit('NORTH-WEST'))
        .when(county.isin(midlands), F.lit('MIDLANDS'))
        .otherwise(F.lit('UNKNOWN'))
    )

    eir = F.col("eircode")
    eir_len = F.length(F.rtrim(eir))  # T-SQL LEN ignores trailing spaces
    eircode_valid = (
        F.when(eir_len == 7, F.lit('Y'))
        .when((eir_len == 8) & (F.substring(eir, 4, 1) == F.lit(' ')), F.lit('Y'))
        .otherwise(F.lit('N'))
    )

    # T-SQL SUBSTRING(x, 0, 2) returns only the first character
    initials = F.upper(F.concat(F.substring(F.col("first_name"), 1, 1), F.substring(F.col("last_name"), 1, 1)))

    out = k.select(
        F.col("customer_id").alias("customer_id"),
        F.rtrim(F.col("first_name")).alias("first_name"),
        F.col("last_name").alias("last_name"),
        F.concat(F.rtrim(F.col("first_name")), F.lit(' '), F.rtrim(F.col("last_name"))).alias("full_name"),
        initials.alias("initials"),
        email.alias("email"),
        F.when(email.isNull(), F.lit(0)).otherwise(email_count).cast("int").alias("email_shared_count"),
        F.col("date_of_birth").alias("date_of_birth"),
        (F.year(F.col("customer_since")) - F.year(F.col("date_of_birth"))).cast("int").alias("age_at_join"),  # LANSH-DEFECT: DATEDIFF(YEAR) counts year boundaries, not completed years of age
        F.col("address_line1").alias("address_line1"),
        F.col("town").alias("town"),
        F.col("county").alias("county"),
        region.alias("region"),
        eir.alias("eircode"),
        eircode_valid.alias("eircode_valid"),
        F.col("segment_code").alias("segment_code"),
        F.when(_ci(F.col("segment_code")) == F.lit('STD'.lower()), F.lit('Y')).otherwise(F.lit('N')).alias("is_standard_segment"),
        F.coalesce(F.col("marketing_opt_in"), F.lit('N')).alias("marketing_opt_in"),
        F.col("customer_since").alias("customer_since"),
        F.upper(F.rtrim(F.col("source_system"))).alias("source_system"),
        F.col("version_count").cast("int").alias("version_count"),
        F.col("updated_at").alias("record_updated_at"),
        F.lit(as_of).alias("as_of_date"),
    )

    return {"dw.dim_customer": out}

defects.intended: Keep the current (latest) version: ORDER BY updated_at DESC, _row_seq DESC, as the comment and CR-1702 describe.
defects.title: Keeps oldest customer version instead of current
defects.what_it_does: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY updated_at, _row_seq) ascending with version_no = 1 keeps each customer's earliest version saved up to @AsOfDate.

defects.intended: The customer's age in completed years on the join date.
defects.title: age_at_join counts calendar-year boundaries
defects.what_it_does: DATEDIFF(YEAR, date_of_birth, customer_since) subtracts the calendar years, so anyone who joined before their birthday that year comes out one year too old.

structured_output.notes:
1. Text comparisons assume the database uses SQL Server's default collation (case-insensitive, accent-sensitive, likely SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS), which also ignores trailing spaces. On that basis the county IN lists, segment_code = 'STD' and the PARTITION BY email in email_shared_count all compare on lower(rtrim(x)). If the legacy database uses a case-sensitive collation, drop the lower().
2. LEN(eircode) is translated as length(rtrim(eircode)), because T-SQL LEN ignores trailing spaces.
3. T-SQL SUBSTRING(x, 0, 2) returns one character, so the translation uses substring(x, 1, 1). Spark's substring(x, 0, 2) would return two characters. This is not marked as a defect because the result is what was intended.
4. UPPER can differ between the engines for a few non-ASCII characters (for example, Java upper-cases ß to SS). This is unlikely to matter for names.
5. Rows with a NULL updated_at are dropped by the date filter, as in the legacy job.
6. version_count counts only the versions saved up to AsOfDate.
7. If first_name or last_name were NULL, the legacy insert would fail on the NOT NULL columns. The translation does not raise an error for this.
8. No trap cards were provided, so traps_handled is empty.
